Prepositional Prefixes

A preposition is a word that is placed before a noun or pronoun to show the relationship between that word and another word in the sentence.  A prefix is an element placed at the beginning of a word to adjust or qualify its meaning.

Adding Emphasis

You can choose to add emphasis on certain words when you want to stress a certain point or call attention to a certain detail. When you pronounce these words, you say them longer and louder than the surrounding words.

Amy: My ears are still ringing.
Vanessa: Yes, that last place was not loud at all. Whatever were they thinking in that place?
Amy: Any seats?
Peter: There were no seats whatsoever. There has got to be someplace less crowded.
Vanessa: It's the football play-offs remember? Everywhere is going to be packed full of football fans.

Peter: Ugh! Football! I'm not interested in the slightest. I wish they would postpone the postseason.
Vanessa: How about that pub called Snakes and Lattes? We could have a game of scrabble while we enjoy our coffee.
Peter: Oh. I do like to play scrabble. I'll even pay for the coffee and the game.
Vanessa: Where the money is coming from, I just don't know.
Peter: As a precaution to you ladies though, I must say, that I'm pretty good at scrabble. So, if we play, I predict my lexical learning will be proven to be superior.

Vanessa: That's because you cheat!
Peter: I don't cheat! I'm just a superb player.
Vanessa: First, you need a translator to translate half the words you spell. Second, your interpretation of the rules is never quite transparent, and finally, tiles have been known to miraculously transfer from the board to your pocket, no one is ever quite sure how or who transported them there. In brief, Peter must be supervised at all times.

Peter: Nah. I'm just a scrabble superstar!
Amy: Hmmm. That's pretty supercilious to make such a prejudgement.
Vanessa: Precisely!
Amy: Surely you are not the scrabble king, are you? So, allow me to postulate another theory. Vanessa and I are going to prevent you from winning by outscoring you.
Peter: To Snakes and Lattes! Post haste!
